title: Run AI Models for Edge Application Development with Just a Few Commands | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA's tutorial shows TensorRT Edge-LLM, a lightweight C++ inference runtime, running Nemotron-3.5 Lightning (30B-A3B, NVFP4) on the new DGX Spark 64GB through the trtedge CLI, including a local OpenAI-compatible server. The same runtime spans development on Spark and deployment on Jetson Thor, DRIVE AGX Thor and IGX Thor. DSpark speculative decoding with three draft tokens lifts mean generation speed from about 73 to 105-127 tokens/s with 27.9GB peak memory.

themes.theme: Edge AI demand and NVIDIA's dev-to-deploy stack

insights.claim: AI is expanding beyond the data center into edge agents that monitor driver attention, help robots plan tasks and coordinate fleets of machines on production lines. These physical AI applications must perceive, reason and act within tight memory, power and latency budgets.
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is positioning edge and physical AI inference as the next growth vector beyond data center GPUs.
insights.quote: These physical AI applications rely on models that perceive, reason, and act within tight memory, power, and latency budgets.

insights.claim: DGX Spark is now available in a 64GB configuration as a platform for embedded developers to prototype, fine-tune and test models and agents. TensorRT Edge-LLM brings the same inference framework to development on Spark and deployment on Jetson Thor, DRIVE AGX Thor and IGX Thor.
insights.so_what: A shared runtime from desktop to embedded Thor platforms deepens lock-in to NVIDIA's software stack across automotive, robotics and medical edge.

insights.claim: Getting a model ready to run at the edge can take substantial setup. NVIDIA's trtedge CLI cuts this to a few commands by downloading the selected model and building TensorRT engines optimized for Spark.
insights.so_what: Lower developer friction is NVIDIA's lever to win embedded AI developers.

insights.claim: The tutorial runs NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4, a text-only model, on Spark. The first launch downloads about 21GB plus an engine build cached in ~/.cache/tensorrt-edgellm, and later launches reuse matching cached engines.
insights.so_what: A 30B-parameter MoE model in 4-bit NVFP4 fits comfortably on a 64GB edge-class device.

insights.so_what: The early 0.x versioning signals that Edge-LLM is still a young product.

insights.claim: DSpark speculative decoding uses a draft model to propose several tokens that the main model verifies in a single pass, and it is enabled through a speculative config with a dedicated Nemotron DSpark draft checkpoint and a tunable num_speculative_tokens.
insights.so_what: Speculative decoding is becoming a standard, configurable knob in edge inference runtimes.

insights.claim: On DGX Spark 64GB, DSpark with three draft tokens raised mean generation speed from 73.4 to 126.9 tokens/s on HumanEval prompts, from 73.3 to 108.5 on SpeedBench 1K and from 72.8 to 105.3 on SpeedBench 2K. Median TTFT was essentially unchanged at about 98, 201-203 and 330 ms respectively.
insights.so_what: Throughput gains of roughly 45-73% come at no latency cost, and code-like prompts benefit most.
insights.speaker: Joe Halabi

insights.claim: Peak total system memory use during DSpark inference was 27.9GB including the OS, measured on DGX OS 7.6.0 with NVFP4, thinking enabled, batch size one and a 128-token output limit.
insights.so_what: Less than half of the 64GB is used, leaving headroom for multiple models or agents on one device.

insights.claim: TensorRT Edge-LLM's supported models include vision-language models that interpret images and video, as well as speech recognition and text-to-speech models, with open Nemotron models and datasets on Hugging Face and Blueprints on build.nvidia.com.
